hypothesis.title: ad service CPU saturation at 94-100% causes 1.5s latency and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors
hypothesis.summary: The ad service's CPU jumped to 94-100% of its limit around 10 minutes before the alert, with 88% throttling reported. This caused ad's p95 latency to spike from 30ms to 1500ms and triggered DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors (561 in logs). Frontend calls to ad became slow (1370ms) and failed, propagating the latency upstream and breaching the frontend p95 SLO. The pattern matches postmortem PM-2026-04-22, where ad CPU saturation caused identical symptoms.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend latency, but frontend is a victim. Traces show frontend calls to ad are slow (1370ms) and failing with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. The ad service's own p95 latency jumped from ~30ms to ~1500ms at -10m, exactly when frontend latency spiked. Ad CPU utilization jumped from ~24% to 94-100% at the same time, with CPUThrottlingHigh (88% throttling) reported. Ad logs show 561 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors and 520 event-loop lag warnings starting at -13m. The email deploy at -5m is a red herring: email is not on the failing trace path (frontend → ad), and the timing doesn't match the -10m spike. The accounting pod restart (exit 137, likely OOMKilled) is also unrelated—accounting is downstream of kafka, not on the frontend path. Postmortem PM-2026-04-22 describes an identical pattern: ad CPU saturation at 97%, p95 ~1.5s, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors, and frontend latency breach. The mechanism is CPU saturation in ad, causing it to process requests slowly and hit client deadlines.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Ad CPU jumped from 24% to 94-100% at -10m, exactly when latency spiked, indicating CPU saturation is the root mechanism.
88% CPU throttling on ad pod confirms the service is being throttled at its limit, directly causing slow request processing.
Ad's own p95 latency jumped from 30ms to 1500ms at -10m, showing ad itself is slow, not just a victim of a downstream dependency.
Failing trace shows the 1370ms delay and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED error originate in the ad service span, confirming ad is the source.
561 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors in ad logs starting at -13m show ad is timing out under load, consistent with CPU saturation.
Ad accounts for 100% of added latency (+720ms) in frontend traces, confirming ad is the latency origin, not frontend itself.

suggested_actions.title: Scale out ad service to 3 replicas to distribute CPU load
suggested_actions.rationale: Immediately reduces CPU pressure per pod. PM-2026-04-22 used this mitigation successfully. Safe and reversible.

suggested_actions.title: Increase ad CPU limit to 500m to reduce throttling
suggested_actions.rationale: Allows ad pods to use more CPU if available on the node. May help if the workload is legitimately higher, but does not address an inefficiency.

suggested_actions.title: Profile ad service to identify CPU hotspot (regex, loop, etc.)
suggested_actions.command: kubectl exec -n otel-demo deployment/ad -- jcmd 1 JFR.start duration=60s filename=/tmp/profile.jfr
suggested_actions.rationale: PM-2026-04-22 found a quadratic regex. Profiling will reveal if a similar code path is burning CPU. Requires follow-up analysis.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Email deployed 2.0.3 at -5m, but the latency spike started at -10m. More importantly, email is not on the failing trace path (frontend → ad); email is only called by checkout, which is not involved in the failing traces.

retrieved_documents.snippet: ## Summary A regex in ad targeting went quadratic on long keyword lists. retrieved_documents.title: CPU saturation and throttling
retrieved_documents.snippet: 1. `kubectl -n otel-demo top pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=<svc>` - at the limit? 2. Was the CPU limit changed recently? `kubectl -n otel-demo get deploy <svc> -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources}'` 3. Mitigate: scale out (`kubectl scale`) or raise the limit (`kubectl set resources`).
